Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray and CT images demonstrate an ill-defined area of consolidation in the left lower lobe (specifically the apical segment) without associated hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. This focal, non-resolving consolidation pattern, particularly when unresponsive to antibiotics and lacking lymph node enlargement, is a classic radiographic presentation of Bronchiolitis Obliterans Organizing Pneumonia (BOOP), distinguishing it from malignancy or sarcoidosis which typically present with lymphadenopathy.
